### Claims

**c1** (20:42-44): God told Musa and his brother to go with His signs and not to slacken in remembering Him, to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed, and to speak to him a gentle word, so that perhaps he would remember or fear.

**c2** (20:45-46): They said that they feared he would hasten against them or transgress; God said they were not to fear, for He was with them both, hearing and seeing.

**c3** (26:10-11): In another passage God called Musa to go to the wrongdoing people, the people of Fir'awn, asking whether they would not be mindful.

**c4** (26:12-14): Musa said that he feared they would deny him, that his chest would be straitened and his tongue not free, and asked God to send to Harun; he said they also had a charge against him, so he feared they would kill him.

**c5** (26:15-17): God said no, and told them both to go with His signs, for He was with them, listening; they were to say that they were the messenger of the Lord of the worlds, and to ask that he send the Children of Israel with them.

**c6** (20:47-48): They were to say that they were the messengers of his Lord, that he should send the Children of Israel with them and not torment them, that they had come with a sign from his Lord, and that peace is on the one who follows the guidance; it had been revealed to them that the punishment is for one who denies and turns away.

**c7** (20:49-50): Fir'awn asked who the Lord of them both was; Musa said that their Lord is He who gave everything its form and then guided.

**c8** (20:51-52): Fir'awn asked about the earlier generations, and Musa said that knowledge of them is with his Lord in a record; his Lord neither errs nor forgets.

**c9** (26:23-28): In another passage Fir'awn asked what the Lord of the worlds is, and Musa answered that He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Lord of their forefathers, and the Lord of the east and the west and what is between them.

**c10** (26:25-29): Fir'awn said to those around him that their messenger who had been sent to them was mad, and told Musa that if he took a god other than him, he would make him one of the imprisoned.

**c11** (79:17-19): Another passage says that Musa was told to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed, and to ask whether he would purify himself, and that Musa would guide him to his Lord so that he would fear.

### One-minute summary

God told Musa and his brother to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed, and speak to him a gentle word, and said He was with them, hearing and seeing [c1][c2]. Fir'awn asked who their Lord was, and Musa answered that He gave everything its form and then guided [c7].

### Complete story

God told Musa and his brother to go with His signs and not to slacken in remembering Him, to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed, and to speak to him a gentle word, so that perhaps he would remember or fear [c1]. They said that they feared he would hasten against them or transgress; God said they were not to fear, for He was with them both, hearing and seeing [c2].

In another passage God called Musa to go to the wrongdoing people, the people of Fir'awn [c3]. Musa said that he feared they would deny him and asked God to send to Harun [c4]. God said no, and told them both to go with His signs, for He was with them, listening [c5]. They were to say that they had come with a sign from his Lord and that he should send the Children of Israel with them and not torment them [c6].

Fir'awn asked who the Lord of them both was; Musa said that their Lord is He who gave everything its form and then guided [c7]. Fir'awn asked about the earlier generations, and Musa said that knowledge of them is with his Lord in a record [c8]. In another passage Fir'awn asked what the Lord of the worlds is, and Musa answered that He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them [c9]. Fir'awn said their messenger was mad, and threatened Musa with prison if he took a god other than him [c10]. Another passage tells Musa to go to Fir'awn and ask whether he would purify himself [c11].

### Deep study

The chapter follows the sending [c1][c2][c3][c4][c5][c11], the words they were to say [c6] and the exchange with Fir'awn [c7][c8][c9][c10]. The sending is told in different passages with different emphasis, one on gentle speech [c1] and one on Musa's fears [c4]. The exchange is told in different forms, with questions about the Lord of them both [c7] and about the Lord of the worlds [c9]. The Arabic of 20:50, rendered here gave everything its form, has more than one possible rendering for scholarly review [c7].

### Kids mode

God told Musa and his brother to go to Fir'awn and to speak gently to him [c1]. God said He was with them, hearing and seeing [c2]. Fir'awn asked who their Lord was, and Musa answered [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the sending begins with a command to speak gently, even to one who has transgressed [c1]. Another is that Musa's fear is met with a promise that God is with them [c2][c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where the meeting took place, how many times it happened, or which passage describes the first meeting.
- Not established: the personal name or period of this Fir'awn. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification with a named ruler of Egypt.
- The wording of 20:50 (everything its form) has more than one possible rendering.
- The passages 20:42-52 and 26:10-29 are read as one sending on matching wording (an inference); the details differ.
- Some passages in the inventory range (7:103-126, 10:75-82) are not used in this shorter record; a reviewer should decide whether to add them.

> **26:49** قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
>
> **26:50** قَالُوا۟ لَا ضَيْرَ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
>
> **26:51** إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَآ أَن كُنَّآ أَوَّلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (26:30-31): Musa asked whether Fir'awn would still not listen if he brought something clear; Fir'awn said to bring it, if he was of the truthful.

**c2** (26:32-33): Musa threw his staff and it was a clear serpent; he drew out his hand and it was white to those looking.

**c3** (26:34-37): Fir'awn told the chiefs around him that this was a learned magician who wanted to drive them from their land with his magic, and asked what they commanded; they said to delay him and his brother and to send gatherers into the cities to bring every learned magician.

**c4** (20:57-59): In another passage Fir'awn asked whether he had come to drive them out of their land with his magic, said that they would bring magic like it, and asked for an appointment; Musa said the appointment was the day of the festival, and that the people were to be gathered at forenoon.

**c5** (26:38-42): The magicians were gathered for the appointed time of a known day; the people were asked whether they would gather, so that they might follow the magicians if they were the victors; the magicians asked Fir'awn whether they would have a reward if they were the victors, and he said yes, and that they would be among those brought near.

**c6** (20:60-61): In another passage Fir'awn turned away, gathered his plan and came; Musa told them not to invent a lie against God, lest He destroy them with a punishment, for whoever invents has failed.

**c7** (26:43-44): Musa told them to throw what they were going to throw; they threw their ropes and staffs and said that by the might of Fir'awn they were the victors.

**c8** (20:65-66): In another passage they asked whether he would throw or they would be the first; he said they should throw, and their ropes and staffs seemed to him, from their magic, to be moving.

**c9** (20:67-69): Musa felt fear within himself; God said that he should not fear, that he was the uppermost, and that he should throw what was in his right hand and it would swallow what they had made, for it was only the trick of a magician.

**c10** (26:45): Musa threw his staff and it swallowed what they fabricated.

**c11** (26:46-48, 20:70): The magicians were cast down in prostration; they said that they believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.

**c12** (26:49, 20:71): Fir'awn said that they had believed him before he gave them permission, that he was their chief who had taught them magic, and threatened to cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and to crucify them.

**c13** (26:50-51): They said that there was no harm, for they would return to their Lord; they hoped He would forgive their faults because they were the first of the believers.

**c14** (20:72-73): In another passage they said that they would never prefer him over the clear proofs that had come to them and over Him who created them, and that he could decree what he decreed, for he decreed only for this worldly life; they had believed so that their Lord would forgive their faults and the magic to which he had compelled them, for God is better and more lasting.

### One-minute summary

Musa threw his staff and it was a clear serpent, and Fir'awn called him a learned magician and gathered the magicians [c2][c3][c5]. When Musa threw his staff it swallowed what they had made, and the magicians were cast down in prostration, saying that they believed in the Lord of Musa and Harun [c10][c11].

### Complete story

Musa asked whether Fir'awn would still not listen if he brought something clear, and Fir'awn said to bring it [c1]. Musa threw his staff and it was a clear serpent; he drew out his hand and it was white to those looking [c2]. Fir'awn told the chiefs that this was a learned magician who wanted to drive them from their land, and they said to send gatherers into the cities to bring every learned magician [c3].

The magicians were gathered for the appointed time of a known day [c5]. In another passage Musa named the day of the festival for the appointment [c4], and Fir'awn gathered his plan and came [c6]. Musa told them to throw what they were going to throw, and they threw their ropes and staffs and said that by the might of Fir'awn they were the victors [c7]. Musa felt fear within himself, and God said that he should not fear, for he was the uppermost [c9]. Musa threw his staff and it swallowed what they fabricated [c10].

The magicians were cast down in prostration; they said that they believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun [c11]. Fir'awn said that they had believed him before he gave them permission, and threatened to cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and to crucify them [c12]. They said that there was no harm, for they would return to their Lord [c13], and in another passage that they would never prefer him over the clear proofs and over Him who created them [c14].

### Deep study

The contest is told in passages that overlap and differ: the appointment and the day of the festival [c4][c5], the throwing [c7][c8], the fear of Musa [c9] and the swallowing of what they had made [c10]. The magicians' belief [c11], Fir'awn's threat [c12] and their reply [c13][c14] close it. The verses do not narrate what became of the magicians after the threat [c12][c13]. One passage records God's word to Musa at his fear [c9].

### Kids mode

Musa threw his staff and it became a snake [c2]. Fir'awn gathered the magicians, and they threw their ropes and staffs [c5][c7]. Musa's staff swallowed what they had made, and the magicians bowed down and said they believed in the Lord of Musa and Harun [c10][c11].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Musa's fear is met with a word from God, not to fear [c9]. Another is that the magicians answer the threat by saying that they will return to their Lord and hope for forgiveness [c13].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how many magicians there were, the place and date of the festival, or the nature of their ropes and staffs beyond that they seemed to move.
- Not established: whether the descriptions of the throwing in 26:43-45 and 20:65-69 describe separate moments.
- The fate of the magicians after the threat is not narrated.
- Not established: how the white hand of 26:33 relates to the other signs; the draft says nothing more about it.
- The verses 20:62-64 (the magicians' private talk) are in the inventory range but not used in this shorter chapter.
